description: Buenos Aires-based card-issuing and payments infrastructure serving 150 clients across 8 LATAM countries, including Santander, BBVA, Bancolombia, Rappi, PicPay, and Western Union. Revenue +250% over the past two years; $160M total raised.
current_status: Deploying Series C into card-issuing enhancements and a flagship global stablecoin card (USDC-native) to address regional inflation/FX volatility. Largest markets Mexico and Brazil; serves embedded-finance builders, neobanks, and large financial institutions.

founder.name: Gastón Irigoyen + ex-MercadoLibre team
founder.background: Founders came out of MercadoLibre — the most successful tech company in LATAM — after operating card-issuing and payments infrastructure at continental scale. Irigoyen was previously at Naranja X and Google Argentina.
founder.problem_fit: EXCEPTIONAL. Built this exact category — payments infrastructure for LATAM — at the only LATAM company that ran it at scale before spinning out.
founder.execution_evidence: Shipped across 8 LATAM countries; 150 enterprise clients including Santander, BBVA, Bancolombia, Rappi, PicPay, Western Union; revenue +250% over 24 months.
founder.red_flags: None on founder fit. Risk is client concentration, not team.

stage_context.vs_base: Pomelo's infrastructure moat (process power + switching costs at the BIN-sponsor level) and 150-client book justify thriving skew (+7pp). Breakout (+6pp) unlock is stablecoin-card expansion beyond LATAM — a genuine first-mover category where Marqeta and Galileo do not yet have shipped product.

verdict: Pomelo survives IF (a) gross-margin per card issued is defensible against Marqeta / Galileo pricing pressure, (b) the stablecoin-card product reaches US-regulatory clarity before Stripe / Nuvei ship competing rails, (c) client concentration (top 5 = likely >40% of revenue) does not tip into a churn event. Most fragile: (c) — infrastructure businesses with concentrated TPV are one enterprise loss away from an 18-month stall.
top_risk: Customer concentration in top-5 enterprise clients; losing Rappi or one of the Santander/BBVA programs removes a large revenue slab with months of warning
top_opportunity: Stablecoin card issuance is a genuine first-mover category for LATAM — correct-by-construction for users who hold USDC and want card utility
